Empirical finding: Target populations were linked to markedly different clinical, community, blood-donor, occupational, and specialized-clinic sampling frames
Appraisal construct: Definition of the intended target population

Empirical finding: Facility-based febrile surveillance and probability-based community surveys used structurally different sampling frames
Appraisal construct: Alignment between the target population and sampling frame

Empirical finding: Recruitment ranged from multistage probability sampling to consecutive, convenience, and incompletely specified non-probability selection
Appraisal construct: Selection of sites, participants, or specimens within the sampling frame

Empirical finding: Some sampling frames and recruitment methods were unclear or insufficiently described
Appraisal construct: Evidentiary sufficiency and reconstructability of population selection

Empirical finding: Unconfirmed IgG, combined IgM/IgG, and IgM serology were common
Appraisal construct: Identification of the primary assay defining the endpoint

Empirical finding: Confirmation pathways included neutralization, molecular testing, sequencing, and multiple-method algorithms
Hybrid serology/direct-detection pathways contained multiple diagnostic components
Appraisal construct: Reconstruction of the complete assay pathway

Empirical finding: Some subsequent tests characterized selected specimens rather than defining the reported endpoint
Appraisal construct: Separation of confirmation, characterization, quality control, and subset testing

Empirical finding: Most article-outcomes presented multiple estimates, complex text, or narrative estimates rather than a numeric proportion
Appraisal construct: Explicit identification of the endpoint-specific numerator and denominator

Empirical finding: Reports frequently included multiple subgroups, time points, assay results, or geographical estimates
Appraisal construct: Rules for distinguishing and reconstructing multiple article-outcomes within a publication

Empirical finding: Endpoint information was distributed across narrative and quantitative fields
Appraisal construct: Documentation of the evidence supporting each appraisal judgment
